prompt: In the Deployment + Service pattern for the tasks-api, what is the Service object's primary job?
choices: Provide a stable network address that routes to any healthy pod matching its selector, regardless of which pods are created or destroyed
Build the Docker image and push it to a registry
Store the application's persistent data on disk

prompt: The tasks-api Deployment is scaled to six replicas, but the app still uses the Tier 3 approach of a single SQLite file on local disk. What actually happens?
choices: Each pod ends up with its own independent, diverging copy of the data instead of six workers sharing one dataset
Kubernetes automatically merges the six SQLite files into one on a shared volume
SQLite detects the replica count and switches itself into a clustered mode

prompt: In the CI/CD pipeline, what does running `kubectl rollout status deployment/tasks-api` as a CI step accomplish?

It deletes the old Deployment immediately so the new one can take its place

prompt: Why does the module's logging middleware emit one JSON object per request instead of a plain-text line like "GET /tasks/1 200 14ms"?

JSON logs take up less disk space than plain text

The Express container has no CPU or memory limits, while the Worker always does

prompt: In the percentage-rollout feature flag implementation, what guarantees that the same user consistently lands on the same side of the `due_dates` flag across multiple requests?

prompt: Why is `kubectl set image deployment/tasks-api tasks-api=<new-image>` safer for production than manually stopping the old container and starting a new one?
choices: Kubernetes performs a rolling update, starting new pods and waiting on their readiness probes before terminating old ones, avoiding a hard all-at-once cutover
